title: Lender to kirana owners and dairy farmers, InPrime Finserv raises Rs 101 crore from FMO, Z47, Pravega
summary: InPrime Finserv raises 101 crore rupees from FMO, Z47, and Pravega
detailed: Bengaluru-based NBFC InPrime Finserv, which lends to small business owners and self-employed people in India's informal economy, has raised Rs 101 crore in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank.
The round takes InPrime's total funding to Rs 190 crore, with the Series B alone accounting for roughly 53% of that.
Its customers are people who are not in formal employment: kirana store owners, dairy farmers, beauty parlour operators and other micro-entrepreneurs.
In July 2025, InPrime raised Rs 50 crore in a Series A1 round led by Pravega Ventures, with Z47, Info Edge Ventures and Kettleborough VC participating.
sentences: Bengaluru-based NBFC InPrime Finserv, which lends to small business owners and self-employed people in India's informal economy, has raised Rs 101 crore in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank.
Existing investors Z47, formerly Matrix Partners India, and Pravega Ventures also took part in the round.
It is FMO's first investment in InPrime.
The round takes InPrime's total funding to Rs 190 crore, with the Series B alone accounting for roughly 53% of that.
It is about twice the size of the startup's previous round.
InPrime said it will use the funding to widen the reach of its existing products and to diversify into micro-mortgage products, in line with what it calls its segment-focused lending approach.
It will also put more money into AI, across agentic AI and co-pilots.
The startup already runs four in-house AI co-pilots that support its credit team, and three AI-powered voice agents that handled more than 1.26 lakh customer calls between April and September 2026.
“ From the beginning, we have believed that prime customers are not limited to the formal economy.

We have been building around the evolving needs of India's informal prime customers by combining engineering, local presence and relevant financial products, ” said Rajat Singh, co-founder and CEO of InPrime Finserv.

Founded in 2021 by former Ujjivan Small Finance Bank executives Sneh Thakur, Manish Raj and Rajat Singh, InPrime operates through STK Credit Private Limited, an RBI-registered NBFC incorporated in Bengaluru in December 2021.
The startup began its lending operations in 2023.
Its customers are people who are not in formal employment: kirana store owners, dairy farmers, beauty parlour operators and other micro-entrepreneurs.

The startup refers to them as the “ informal prime ” segment, borrowers who run established businesses and are creditworthy but struggle to get loans because of the way traditional lenders assess risk.

According to InPrime, its technology lets it underwrite such borrowers by interpreting unstructured data, understanding customers beyond conventional financial metrics, and delivering services at scale in vernacular languages.
InPrime now operates 46 area offices across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Madhya Pradesh.
It has served more than 27,000 households and disbursed Rs 516.92 crore in loans to date.
As of 30 September 2026, its assets under management stood at Rs 332.8 crore, with gross non-performing assets of 0.80%.
That works out to roughly Rs 2.7 crore of bad loans on its books.
The numbers have risen sharply since its last fundraise.
In July 2025, InPrime raised Rs 50 crore in a Series A1 round led by Pravega Ventures, with Z47, Info Edge Ventures and Kettleborough VC participating.
At that point it had served over 7,500 households and disbursed nearly Rs 100 crore.
That means cumulative disbursements have grown about five times, and households served about 3.6 times, in roughly 16 months.
At the time of the Series A1, InPrime said it planned to expand to 50 locations across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana within a year.
It has since added Uttarakhand and Madhya Pradesh.
Its other backers include Info Edge Ventures, Kettleborough VC and Titan Capital.
FMO is a public-private development bank supervised by the Dutch central bank, with investments spanning more than 85 countries, according to the institution.
“ Expanding access to finance for underserved entrepreneurs and households is closely aligned with FMO's aim of making finance more inclusive and accessible.

InPrime's combination of technology, data-driven underwriting, and local presence provides an opportunity to reach customers who are often overlooked by traditional lenders, ” said Peter Byrde, Director Private Equity at FMO.
The InPrime deal adds to FMO's exposure to Indian lenders that serve small borrowers.
In January this year, it committed $30 million to Annapurna Finance, a microfinance institution, through listed non-convertible debentures.
Annapurna serves 2.9 million clients across 21 states through 1,708 branches, and 98% of its borrowers are women, according to FMO.
